title.zh: 卷四十五 志第二十六: 刑
title.raw: 卷四十五 志第二十六: 刑 Volume 45 Treatises 26: Punishment

sentences.zh: 昔者先王因人之知畏而作刑，因人之知恥而作法。

translations.literal: In antiquity the former kings, because people knew fear, established punishments; because people knew shame, they established laws.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times, the former kings instituted punishments in response to humanity's capacity for fear, and established laws in response to humanity's capacity for shame.

sentences.zh: 畏也、恥也，五性之良知，七情之大閑也。

translations.literal: Fear and shame are the innate knowledge of the five natures and the great restraint of the seven emotions.
translations.idiomatic: Fear and shame are the innate moral sense within the five inherent dispositions and the great boundary restraining the seven emotions.

sentences.zh: 是故，刑以治已然，法以禁未然，畏以處小人，恥以遇君子。

translations.literal: Therefore punishments govern what has already happened, laws restrain what has not yet happened, fear handles petty men, shame treats noble men.
translations.idiomatic: Thus punishments address what has already occurred, laws prevent what has not yet occurred, fear governs petty men, and shame governs noble men.

sentences.zh: 君子知恥，小人知畏，天下平矣！

translations.literal: When noble men know shame and petty men know fear, all under Heaven is at peace!
translations.idiomatic: When the noble know shame and the petty know fear, the realm is at peace.

sentences.zh: 是故先王養其威而用之，畏可以教愛。

translations.literal: Therefore the former kings nurtured their authority and employed it; fear can teach love.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the former kings cultivated their authority and put it to use, for fear can teach one to love.

sentences.zh: 慎其法而行之，恥可以立廉。

translations.literal: They were careful with their laws and carried them out; shame can establish integrity.
translations.idiomatic: They handled their laws with care and enforced them, for shame can establish integrity.

sentences.zh: 愛以興仁，廉以興義，仁義興，刑法不幾於措乎？

translations.literal: Love gives rise to benevolence, integrity gives rise to righteousness; when benevolence and righteousness flourish, would punishments and laws not nearly fall into disuse?
translations.idiomatic: Love engenders benevolence, integrity engenders righteousness; when benevolence and righteousness flourish, punishments and laws would nearly become unnecessary, would they not?

sentences.zh: 金初，法制簡易，無輕重貴賤之別，刑、贖並行，此可施諸新國，非經世久遠之規也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin, legal institutions were simple and crude, with no distinction between light and heavy or noble and base; corporal punishment and ransoms were applied in parallel. This could be applied in a new state but was not a regulation for long-lasting governance of the world.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jin, the legal system was rudimentary, with no gradations of severity or rank; physical punishment and commutation by payment operated side by side. Such measures might suit a newly founded state, but they were no model for enduring governance.

sentences.zh: 天會以來，漸從吏議，皇統頒制，兼用古律。

translations.literal: From the Tianhui era onward, they gradually followed officials' recommendations; Huangtong promulgated regulations, using ancient statutes together.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tianhui period onward, policy gradually followed officials' counsel; under Huangtong, regulations were promulgated that incorporated elements of older penal codes.

sentences.zh: 厥後，正隆又有《續降制書》。

translations.literal: Thereafter, in Zhenglong there was again the Continued Promulgated Regulatory Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Later, under Zhenglong, there appeared the Continued Promulgated Regulatory Documents.

sentences.zh: 大定有《權宜條理》，有《重修制條》。

translations.literal: In Dading there were the Provisional Articles and Ordinances and the Recast Regulatory Articles.
translations.idiomatic: The Dading era produced the Provisional Articles and Ordinances and the Recast Regulatory Articles.

sentences.zh: 明昌之世，《律義》、《敕條》並修，品式當浸備。

translations.literal: In the Mingchang era, the Legal Commentaries and Imperial Decree Articles were both revised, and categories and forms should have gradually become complete.
translations.idiomatic: During the Mingchang reign, the Legal Commentaries and Imperial Decree Articles were both revised, and the classification of offenses should have grown increasingly comprehensive.

sentences.zh: 既而《泰和律義》成書，宜無遺憾。

translations.literal: Subsequently the Tahe Legal Commentaries were completed as a book; there ought to have been no regrets.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tahe Legal Commentaries were finally completed, nothing should have been left wanting.

sentences.zh: 然國脈紓蹙，風俗醇樗，世道升降，君子觀一代之刑法，每有以先知焉。

translations.literal: Yet the nation's life-thread was slack and constricted, customs were pure but blunt, the age's way rose and fell; noble men observing a generation's penal laws often had grounds for foreknowledge.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as the dynasty's vital force waned and customs grew rustic, as the moral climate shifted, learned observers who studied a generation's penal code could often read in advance which way the realm was headed.

sentences.zh: 金法以杖折徒，累及二百，州縣立威，甚者置刃於杖，虐於肉刑。

translations.literal: Jin law used the staff to commute penal servitude, accumulating up to two hundred strokes; prefectures and counties established authority, and in extreme cases they placed blades on the staff, more cruel than corporal punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Jin law permitted beating with staffs to substitute for penal servitude, with strokes accumulating to as many as two hundred; local officials used this to assert their authority, and in the worst cases they fitted blades to the staffs, making the punishment more brutal than dismemberment itself.

sentences.zh: 季年，君臣好用筐篋故習，由是以深文傅致為能吏，以慘酷辦事為長才。

translations.literal: In the dynasty's final years, ruler and ministers readily favored old habits of petty graft; thereby making severe legal construction the mark of a capable official and handling affairs with brutality the sign of great talent.
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's closing years, court and ministers alike fell back on petty corruption as custom; officials who twisted the law to secure convictions passed as men of ability, and those who handled cases with cruelty passed as men of outstanding talent.

sentences.zh: 百司奸贓真犯，此可決也，而微過亦然。

translations.literal: For true offenses of corruption among the hundred offices this could be decided, yet minor faults were treated the same.
translations.idiomatic: Flagrant corruption among the bureaucracy warranted decisive punishment, yet even minor infractions were punished just as harshly.

sentences.zh: 風紀之臣，失糾皆決。

translations.literal: Officials charged with upholding standards—any failure in correction was decided by corporal punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Even censors responsible for discipline were beaten for any failure to correct wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 考滿，校其受決多寡以為殿最。

translations.literal: At the end of their term of evaluation, they compared how many punishments each had received to determine ranking from lowest to highest.
translations.idiomatic: At term's end, officials were ranked according to how many beating sentences they had imposed—more strokes meant a better evaluation.

sentences.zh: 原其立法初意，欲以同疏戚、壹小大，使之咸就繩約於律令之中，莫不齊手並足以聽公上之所為，蓋秦人強主威之意也。

translations.literal: Investigating the original intent of their legislation, they wished to make kinship bonds uniform, make great and small one, cause all to submit to constraint within statutes and ordinances, none not leveling hands and joining feet to heed what the public authority did—essentially the intent of Qin men to strengthen the ruler's authority.
translations.idiomatic: The original intent behind their legislation was to erase distinctions of kinship and rank, to force everyone alike into the constraints of statute, to make all stand with hands level and feet aligned, awaiting whatever the throne commanded—essentially the Qin ideal of concentrating sovereign power.

sentences.zh: 是以待宗室少恩，待大夫士少禮。

translations.literal: Therefore they treated the imperial clan with little kindness and treated great officers and scholars with little ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the court showed scant kindness toward the imperial clan and scant ritual deference toward the official elite.

sentences.zh: 終金之代，忍恥以就功名，雖一時名士有所不免。

translations.literal: Throughout the Jin dynasty, men endured shame to pursue fame and achievement; even renowned figures of the day were not exempt.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Jin dynasty, men endured humiliation to advance their careers, and even the most celebrated scholars of the age were not spared.

sentences.zh: 至於避辱遠引，罕聞其人。

translations.literal: As for avoiding disgrace and withdrawing far away, one rarely heard of such persons.
translations.idiomatic: Men who withdrew from office to avoid disgrace were exceedingly rare.

sentences.zh: 殊不知君子無恥而犯義，則小人無畏而犯刑矣。

translations.literal: They did not realize that when noble men are without shame and violate righteousness, then petty men are without fear and violate punishments.
translations.idiomatic: They failed to see that when the noble lose their sense of shame and transgress moral duty, the petty lose their fear and transgress the penal code.

sentences.zh: 是故論者於教愛立廉之道，往往致太息之意焉。

translations.literal: Therefore commentators on the way of teaching love and establishing integrity often expressed deep sighs.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason, commentators who reflected on the path of teaching love and establishing integrity often could only sigh in regret.

sentences.zh: 雖然，世宗臨御，法司奏讞，或去律援經，或揆義制法。

translations.literal: Nevertheless, when Shizong took the throne, the legal offices reported cases for judgment; sometimes they departed from statutes and appealed to the classics, sometimes they measured meaning to formulate law.
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless, under Emperor Shizong's reign, when legal offices reported cases for judgment, they sometimes set aside the code to appeal to the classics, and sometimes fashioned law by weighing moral principle.

sentences.zh: 近古人君聽斷，言幾於道，鮮有及之者。

translations.literal: Among recent ancient rulers' hearing and deciding cases, his words nearly reached the Way; few could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Among rulers of recent antiquity in hearing and deciding cases, his pronouncements came close to the Way itself; few could equal him.

sentences.zh: 章宗、宣宗嘗親民事，當寧裁決，寬猛出入雖時或過中，跡其矜恕之多，猶有祖風焉。

translations.literal: Zhangzong and Xuanzong at times personally handled civil affairs, deciding cases at the imperial seat; leniency and severity in their departures sometimes exceeded the mean, yet tracing their many acts of compassion and pardon, there was still ancestral style.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Zhangzong and Xuanzong sometimes took civil cases in hand themselves, rendering judgment from the throne; though their leniency and severity occasionally overshot the mark, the record of their compassion and clemency still bore traces of their forebears' style.

sentences.zh: 簡牘所存，可為高抬貴手者，《本紀》、《刑志》詳略互見云。

translations.literal: What survives in documents that can be held up for high regard: the Basic Annals and the Treatise on Punishment show detail and summary complementing each other.
translations.idiomatic: What survives in the written record worthy of note may be found in the Basic Annals and this Treatise on Punishment, where detail and summary complement each other throughout.

sentences.zh: 金國舊俗，輕罪笞以柳篸，殺人及盜劫者，擊其腦殺之，沒其家貲，以十之四入官，其六償主，並以家人為奴婢。

translations.literal: Jin state's old custom: light offenses were flogged with willow switches; killers and robbers were struck on the brain and killed, their household property confiscated, four-tenths entering the government, six-tenths compensating the victim, and their household members all made slaves and maidservants.
translations.idiomatic: By Jin custom, minor offenses were punished with flogging using willow switches; murderers and robbers were struck on the head and killed, their household property confiscated, with four-tenths going to the state and six-tenths to compensate the victim, while all members of the household were enslaved.

sentences.zh: 其親屬欲以馬牛雜物贖者從之。

translations.literal: If their kin wished to ransom them with horses, cattle, and miscellaneous goods, this was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives who wished to ransom them with horses, cattle, or other goods were permitted to do so.

sentences.zh: 或重罪亦聽自贖，然恐無辨于齊民，則劓、刵以為別。

translations.literal: Even serious offenses were sometimes permitted self-ransom, yet fearing no distinction from common people, they used nose-cutting and ear-cutting as marks of differentiation.
translations.idiomatic: Even serious offenses sometimes allowed self-ransom, but lest offenders be indistinguishable from ordinary folk, they were marked by cutting off the nose or ears.

sentences.zh: 其獄則掘地深廣數丈為之。

translations.literal: Their prisons were made by digging earth several zhang deep and wide.
translations.idiomatic: Prisons were pits dug several zhang deep and wide in the earth.

sentences.zh: 太宗雖承太祖無變舊風之訓，亦稍用遼、宋法。

translations.literal: Taizong, though inheriting Taizu's instruction not to change old customs, also slightly used Liao and Song law.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong, though he inherited Taizu's injunction to preserve old customs unchanged, also drew somewhat on Liao and Song legal practice.

sentences.zh: 天會七年，詔凡竊盜，但得物徒三年，十貫以上徒五年，刺字充下軍，三十貫以上終身，仍以贓滿盡命刺字於面，五十貫以上死，征償如舊制。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianhui, an edict: for all theft, if goods were obtained, penal servitude three years; ten strings or more, penal servitude five years, tattooed characters and assigned to the lower army; thirty strings or more, for life, and when stolen goods reached the full amount, ordered tattooed on the face; fifty strings or more, death, collection of compensation as in the old system.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianhui, an edict decreed that any thief who obtained goods would serve three years at penal labor; ten strings or more warranted five years, tattooing, and assignment to the lower army; thirty strings or more meant lifelong servitude, with full-value thefts tattooed on the face; fifty strings or more meant death, with compensation collected as under the old system.

sentences.zh: 熙宗天眷元年十月，禁親王以下佩刀入宮。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Tianjuan under Xizong, princes of the blood and below were forbidden to wear swords when entering the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Tianjuan under Emperor Xizong, imperial princes and those below them were forbidden to carry swords into the palace.

sentences.zh: 衛禁之法，實自此始。

translations.literal: Palace guard prohibitions in fact began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Palace security regulations in fact date from this decree.

sentences.zh: 三年，復取河南地，乃詔其民，約所用刑法皆從律文，罷獄卒酷毒刑具，以從寬恕。

translations.literal: In the third year, having recovered the Henan territory, they then edicted its people that the criminal law to be applied should all follow statutory text, abolishing jailers' cruel and poisonous instruments of punishment to follow leniency and pardon.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, after recovering the Henan region, the court edicted its inhabitants that all criminal law applied there should follow statutory text, abolishing jailers' cruel instruments of torture in favor of lenient treatment.

sentences.zh: 至皇統間，詔諸臣，以本朝舊制，兼采隋、唐之制，參遼、宋之法。

translations.literal: By the Huangtong period, they edicted the various ministers to take this dynasty's old system, together adopt Sui and Tang systems, and reference Liao and Song law.
translations.idiomatic: By the Huangtong period, ministers were commanded to compile law drawing on the dynasty's own old institutions, incorporating elements of Sui and Tang practice and referencing Liao and Song codes.

sentences.zh: 類以成書，名曰《皇統制》，頒行中外。

translations.literal: They were classified to complete a book, named the Huangtong Regulations, and promulgated within and without.
translations.idiomatic: These were classified into a completed code named the Huangtong Regulations and promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 時制，杖罪至百，則臀、背分決。

translations.literal: At that time the system was: for staff punishment up to one hundred strokes, buttocks and back were decided separately.
translations.idiomatic: Under that system, when a beating sentence reached one hundred strokes, the blows were divided between buttocks and back.

sentences.zh: 及海陵庶人以脊近心腹，遂禁之，雖主決奴牌，亦論以違制。

translations.literal: When Hailing the commoner [usurper], because the back is near the heart and belly, then forbade it; even when masters decided punishment on slave tablets, it was still judged as violating regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When the usurper Hailing took power, he forbade back strokes because the back lies near the vital organs; even when masters punished slaves by tablet, back strokes were treated as a violation of regulations.

sentences.zh: 又多變易舊制，至正隆間，著為《續降制書》，與《皇統制》並行焉。

translations.literal: He also changed the old system in many ways; by the Zhenglong period it was written as the Continued Promulgated Regulatory Documents, applied in parallel with the Huangtong Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He also altered the old system in many respects; by the Zhenglong period these were codified as the Continued Promulgated Regulatory Documents, applied alongside the Huangtong Regulations.

sentences.zh: 然二君任情用法，自有異於是者矣。

translations.literal: Yet the two rulers applied law according to whim, naturally having differences from this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet both rulers applied the law as whim dictated, often departing from what the codes prescribed.

sentences.zh: 及世宗即位，以正隆之亂，盜賊公行，兵甲未息，一時制旨多從時宜，遂集為《軍前權宜條理》。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, because of the Zhenglong turmoil, bandits walked openly, arms and armor had not ceased; temporary regulatory edicts mostly followed timely fitness, and were then collected as the Provisional Articles and Ordinances Before the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong ascended the throne, amid the chaos of the Zhenglong period, with bandits roaming freely and warfare still unsettled, many temporary edicts followed expedient needs and were collected as the Provisional Articles and Ordinances Before the Army.

sentences.zh: 大定四年，尚書省奏：「大興民男子李十、婦人楊仙哥並以亂言當斬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dading, the Secretariat memorialized: 'Daxing commoner, male Li Shi and woman Yang Xian'ge, both for disorderly speech should be beheaded.'
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dading, the Secretariat reported: 'The Daxing commoners Li Shi, a man, and Yang Xian'ge, a woman, have both spoken disorderly words and should be beheaded.'

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「愚民不識典法，有司亦未嘗丁寧誥戒，豈可遽加極刑。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Foolish commoners do not know canonical law; the responsible offices also have never earnestly admonished and warned—how can we hastily apply extreme punishment?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'These foolish commoners do not know the law, and the responsible offices have never earnestly warned them—how can we hastily impose the death penalty?'

sentences.zh: 」以減死論。

translations.literal: They were sentenced with commuted death.
translations.idiomatic: They were sentenced to commuted death instead.

sentences.zh: 五年，命有司復加刪定《條理》，與前《制書》兼用。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he ordered the responsible offices again to revise and fix the Articles and Ordinances, to be used together with the previous Regulatory Documents.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, he ordered officials to revise the Articles and Ordinances again for use alongside the earlier Regulatory Documents.

sentences.zh: 七年，左藏庫夜有盜殺都監郭良臣盜金珠，求盜不得。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, at night in the Left Treasury there was a thief who killed Director Guo Liangchen and stole gold and pearls; the thief could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, a thief broke into the Left Treasury at night, killed the director Guo Liangchen, and stole gold and pearls, but the culprit could not be found.

sentences.zh: 命點檢司治之，執其可疑者八人鞫之，掠三人死，五人誣伏。

translations.literal: He ordered the Inspection Office to handle it; they seized eight suspicious persons and interrogated them, torturing three to death, five falsely confessing.
translations.idiomatic: The Inspection Office was ordered to investigate; eight suspects were seized and interrogated, three dying under torture and five falsely confessing.

sentences.zh: 上疑之，命同知大興府事移剌道雜治。

translations.literal: The emperor was suspicious and ordered Associate Administrator of Daxing Prefecture Yila Dao to conduct a mixed investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew suspicious and ordered Yila Dao, associate administrator of Daxing Prefecture, to conduct a separate investigation.

sentences.zh: 既而親軍百夫長阿思缽鬻金於市，事覺，伏誅。

translations.literal: Subsequently an imperial guard centurion Asibo sold gold in the market; the matter was discovered and he submitted to execution.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward an imperial guard centurion named Asibo was discovered selling gold in the market; the crime was exposed and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 上聞之曰：「箠楚之下，何求不得，奈何鞫獄者不以情求之乎？

translations.literal: On hearing this the emperor said: 'Under the rod and whip, what cannot be obtained? Why do those who interrogate prisoners not seek according to the facts?'
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this the emperor said: 'Under the rod and whip, what confession cannot be extracted? Why do interrogators not seek the truth according to the facts?'

sentences.zh: 」賜死者錢人二百貫，不死者五十貫。

translations.literal: He bestowed on the dead two hundred strings of cash per person, on those not dead fifty strings.
translations.idiomatic: He granted two hundred strings of cash to the families of the dead and fifty strings to the survivors.

sentences.zh: 於是禁護衛百夫長、五十夫長非直日不得帶刀入宮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he forbade guard centurions and half-centurions, unless on daily duty, from carrying swords into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon centurions and half-centurions of the guard were forbidden to carry swords into the palace except on their assigned duty days.

sentences.zh: 是歲，斷死囚二十人。

translations.literal: That year, twenty death-row prisoners were decided.
translations.idiomatic: That year, twenty prisoners were sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 八年，製品官犯賭博法，贓不滿五十貫者其法杖，聽贖。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he regulated that officials of rank who violated the gambling law, when stolen goods did not reach fifty strings, should by law receive the staff, with redemption permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, regulations were issued that ranked officials who violated gambling laws, when the stakes did not reach fifty strings, would receive beating by law with commutation permitted.

sentences.zh: 再犯者杖之。

translations.literal: Repeat offenders were staff-punished.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat offenders were beaten.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「杖者所以罰小人也。

translations.literal: Moreover he said: 'The staff is what is used to punish petty men.'
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'The staff is the punishment reserved for petty men.'

sentences.zh: 既為職官，當先廉恥，既無廉恥，故以小人之罰罰之。

translations.literal: Since they are already office-holders, they should first have integrity and shame; since they have no integrity and shame, therefore they are punished with petty men's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Since they hold office, they should possess integrity and shame; lacking both, they are punished with the penalty reserved for petty men.'

sentences.zh: 」九年，因御史臺奏獄事，上曰：「近聞法官或各執所見，或觀望宰執之意，自今制無正條者皆以律文為准。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, because the Censorate reported prison affairs, the emperor said: 'Recently I have heard that judges sometimes each cling to their own views, sometimes watch and wait for the chief ministers' intent—from now on where regulations have no proper article, all shall take statutory text as standard.'
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when the Censorate reported on prison affairs, the emperor said: 'I have lately heard that judges sometimes cling to their own views or watch for the chief ministers' intent—from now on, wherever regulations lack a proper article, the statutory text shall be the standard.'

sentences.zh: 」復命杖至百者臀、背分受，如舊法。

translations.literal: He again ordered that when staff reached one hundred, buttocks and back should receive separately, as in the old law.
translations.idiomatic: He also restored the old rule that when a beating reached one hundred strokes, the blows were divided between buttocks and back.

sentences.zh: 已而，上謂宰臣曰：「朕念罪人杖不分受，恐至深重，乃令復舊。

translations.literal: Shortly after, the emperor told the chief ministers: 'I considered that when criminals' staff was not received separately, I feared it would reach too deep and heavy, and therefore ordered restoration of the old way.'
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, the emperor told his chief ministers: 'I had feared that when beating was not divided between buttocks and back, the injury would be too severe, and so I restored the old practice.'

sentences.zh: 今聞民間有不欲者，其令罷之。

translations.literal: Now I hear that among the people there are those who do not wish it—let this be ordered abolished.'
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear that the people do not want it—let it be abolished.'

sentences.zh: 」十年，尚書省奏：「河中府張錦自言復父仇，法當死。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the Secretariat memorialized: 'Hezhong Prefecture's Zhang Jin himself stated he avenged his father's enmity; by law he should die.'
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, the Secretariat reported: 'Zhang Jin of Hezhong Prefecture has declared that he avenged his father's death; by law he should die.'

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「彼復父仇，又自言之，烈士也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'He avenged his father's enmity and moreover spoke of it himself—a man of fierce integrity.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'He avenged his father and confessed it himself—he is a man of fierce integrity.'

sentences.zh: 以減死論。

translations.literal: He was sentenced with commuted death.
translations.idiomatic: He was sentenced to commuted death instead.

sentences.zh: 」十一年，詔諭有司曰：「應司獄廨舍須近獄安置，囚禁之事常親提控，其獄卒必選年深而信實者輪直。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, an edict instructed the responsible offices: 'Prison offices' quarters must be placed near the prison; matters of imprisonment should be personally supervised in control; prison guards must be selected from those of long years who are trustworthy and sincere, rotating duty.'
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, an edict instructed officials: 'Prison offices must be located near the jail; imprisonment must be personally supervised; and jailers must be chosen from experienced, trustworthy men serving in rotation.'

sentences.zh: 」十二年，尚書省言：「內丘令蒲察台補自科部內錢立德政碑，復有其餘錢二百餘貫，罪當 除名。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the Secretariat stated: 'Neiqiu magistrate Pucha Taibu, from funds within his department, erected a merit stele, and moreover had over two hundred strings remaining; the offense warrants dismissal from office.'
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, the Secretariat reported: 'Pucha Taibu, magistrate of Neiqiu, used departmental funds to erect a merit stele and kept over two hundred strings besides; the offense warrants dismissal from office.'

sentences.zh: 今遇赦當敘，仍免徵贓。

translations.literal: Now encountering an amnesty he should be reappointed, and still be exempted from collecting stolen goods.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty now entitles him to reinstatement, with confiscation waived.'

sentences.zh: 」上以貪偽，勿敘，且曰：「乞取之贓，若有赦原，予者何辜？

translations.literal: The emperor, because of greedy falsity, forbade reappointment, and moreover said: 'For stolen goods obtained by begging and taking, if there is amnesty and pardon, what guilt do the givers have?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, deeming this greedy fraud, forbade reinstatement and said: 'If stolen goods obtained by extortion are pardoned by amnesty, what wrong have the victims done?'

sentences.zh: 自今可並追還其主，惟應入官者免徵。

translations.literal: From now on all may together be pursued and returned to their owners; only what should enter the government is exempted from collection.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth such goods must all be returned to their owners; only what should go to the state may be exempted from collection.'

sentences.zh: 」尚書省奏，盜有發塚者，上曰：「功臣墳墓亦有被發者，蓋無告捕之賞，故人無所畏。

translations.literal: The Secretariat memorialized that there were thieves who opened tombs; the emperor said: 'Meritorious officials' graves also have been opened—probably because there is no reward for reporting and capturing, so people have nothing to fear.'
translations.idiomatic: When the Secretariat reported tomb robberies, the emperor said: 'Even the graves of meritorious officials have been opened—probably because there is no reward for reporting and capturing them, so people have nothing to fear.'

sentences.zh: 自今告得實者量與給賞。

translations.literal: From now on those who report and it is verified shall be given rewards in measured amount.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth informants whose reports prove true shall receive rewards in proportion.'

sentences.zh: 」故咸平尹石抹阿沒剌以贓死於獄，上謂：「其不屍諸市已為厚幸。

translations.literal: Former Xianping Administrator Shimou Amela died in prison for corruption; the emperor said: 'That his corpse was not exposed in the market was already thick favor.'
translations.idiomatic: The former administrator of Xianping, Shimou Amela, died in prison for corruption; the emperor remarked: 'That his corpse was not exposed in the marketplace was already great leniency.'

sentences.zh: 貧窮而為盜賊，蓋不得已。

translations.literal: Being poor and becoming bandits and thieves is probably unavoidable necessity.
translations.idiomatic: Men who turn to banditry out of poverty do so from necessity.'

sentences.zh: 三品職官以贓至死，愚亦甚矣！

translations.literal: A third-rank office-holder dying for corruption—how extremely foolish!
translations.idiomatic: But for a third-rank official to die for corruption—how profoundly foolish!'

sentences.zh: 其諸子可皆除名。

translations.literal: His various sons may all be dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: All his sons shall be dismissed from office.'

sentences.zh: 」先是，詔自今除名人子孫有在仕者並取奏裁。

translations.literal: Earlier, an edict had stated that from now on dismissed persons' descendants who held office should all be submitted for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, an edict had decreed that henceforth the sons of dismissed officials who held office must all be submitted for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 十三年，詔立春後、立秋前，及大祭祀，月朔、望，上、下弦，二十四氣，雨未晴，夜未明，休暇並禁屠宰日，皆不聽決死刑，惟強盜則不待秋後。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, an edict: after Beginning of Spring and before Beginning of Autumn, and great sacrifices, new and full moons, first and last quarters, the twenty-four qi, when rain had not cleared, when night had not brightened, rest days and forbidden slaughter days—all did not permit deciding capital punishment, except bandits and robbers who need not wait until after autumn.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, an edict forbade capital sentences from after Beginning of Spring until before Beginning of Autumn, and also on days of great sacrifice, new and full moons, quarter moons, the twenty-four seasonal nodes, rainy days, before dawn, holidays, and days when slaughter was forbidden—except for armed robbers, who need not wait until autumn.

sentences.zh: 十五年，詔有司曰：「朕惟人命至重，而在制竊盜贓至五十貫者處死，自今可令至八十貫者處死。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, an edict to the responsible offices: 'I consider human life supremely heavy; yet in the regulations, theft with stolen goods reaching fifty strings is punished with death—from now on it may be ordered that reaching eighty strings is punished with death.'
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, the emperor edicted officials: 'I hold human life supremely precious; yet the regulations execute thieves when stolen goods reach fifty strings—from now on let the threshold be eighty strings.'

sentences.zh: 」十七年，陳言者乞設提刑司，以糾諸路刑獄之失。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, memorializers requested establishing a Office for Elevating Punishments to correct errors in penal prisons on the various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, memorialists requested establishing an office to supervise punishments and correct errors in prisons on the various circuits.

sentences.zh: 尚書省議，以謂久恐滋弊。

translations.literal: The Secretariat deliberated, considering that in the long run they feared breeding abuses.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat deliberated that such an office would breed abuses over time.

sentences.zh: 上乃命距京師數千里外懷冤上訴者，集其事以待選官就問。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered that those bearing grievances and appealing who were several thousand li from the capital should have their matters collected to await selection of officials to go and inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instead ordered that grievants appealing from thousands of li beyond the capital should have their cases collected pending dispatch of selected officials to investigate on site.

sentences.zh: 時濟南尹梁肅言，犯徒者當免杖。

translations.literal: At that time Jinan Administrator Liang Su stated that those who committed penal servitude should be exempted from the staff.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liang Su, administrator of Jinan, proposed that those sentenced to penal servitude should be exempted from beating.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以為今法已輕于古，恐滋奸惡，不從。

translations.literal: The court considered that present law was already lighter than antiquity, fearing it would breed wickedness and evil, and did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that current law was already more lenient than antiquity and feared encouraging wickedness, and did not adopt the proposal.

sentences.zh: 嘗詔宰臣，朝廷每歲再遣審錄官，本以為民伸冤滯也，而所遣多不盡心，但文具而已。

translations.literal: He once edicted the chief ministers: 'The court each year twice dispatches review and record officials, originally to extend grievances and delays for the people, yet those dispatched mostly do not exhaust their hearts, but only go through the forms.'
translations.idiomatic: He once told his chief ministers: 'The court dispatches review officials twice each year precisely to redress the people's grievances, yet those dispatched mostly fail to apply themselves and merely go through the motions.'

sentences.zh: 審錄之官，非止理問重刑，凡訴訟案牘，皆當閱實是非，囚徒不應囚繫則當釋放，官吏之罪即以狀聞，失糾察者嚴加懲斷，不以贖論。

translations.literal: Review and record officials should not only manage and inquire into heavy punishments; all litigation case documents should have their right and wrong examined in fact; prisoners who should not be imprisoned should be released; officials' offenses should be reported by memorial; those who fail in correction and inspection should be strictly punished and decided, not judged by ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Review officials should not limit themselves to capital cases; they must examine the merits of all litigation, release prisoners who should not be held, report officials' offenses by memorial, and punish failures of oversight severely, without commutation.

sentences.zh: 又以監察御史體察東北路官吏，輒受訟牒，為不稱職，笞之五十。

translations.literal: Also because a surveillance censor investigating Dongbei Road officials readily accepted litigation documents, as unfit for office, he was given fifty strokes of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: A surveillance censor investigating officials on the Northeast Circuit was beaten fifty strokes for improperly accepting litigation documents, deeming him unfit for office.

sentences.zh: 又謂宰臣曰：「比聞大理寺斷獄，雖無疑者亦經旬月，何耶？

translations.literal: He again told the chief ministers: 'Recently I have heard that the Court of Judicial Review decides cases—even those without doubt also take ten days or a month—why?'
translations.idiomatic: He again told his chief ministers: 'I have lately heard that the Court of Judicial Review takes ten days or a month even for cases without doubt—why is this?'

sentences.zh: 」參知政事移剌道對曰：「在法，決死囚不過七日，徒刑五日，杖罪三日。

translations.literal: Vice Councilor Yila Dao replied: 'By law, deciding death prisoners does not exceed seven days, penal servitude five days, staff offenses three days.'
translations.idiomatic: Vice Councilor Yila Dao replied: 'By law, capital cases must be decided within seven days, penal servitude within five, and beating offenses within three.'

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「法有程限，而輒違之，弛慢也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'The law has time limits, yet they readily violate them—this is lax slowness.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'The law sets time limits, yet they violate them at will—this is negligence.'

sentences.zh: 」罷朝，御批送尚書省曰：「凡法寺斷重輕罪各有期限，法官但犯皆的決，豈敢有違。

translations.literal: After court was dismissed, an imperial annotation was sent to the Secretariat: 'All judicial offices deciding heavy and light offenses each have time limits; judges, for any offense, all have definite decisions—how would they dare violate?'
translations.idiomatic: After court, an imperial annotation was sent to the Secretariat: 'Every judicial office has time limits for deciding offenses of every severity; judges must render definitive judgments for every case—how dare they violate these limits?'

sentences.zh: 但以卿等所見不一，至於再三批送，其議定奏者書奏牘亦不下旬日，以致事多滯留，自今當勿復爾。

translations.literal: But because you all have differing views, reaching to repeated annotations and returns, those whose deliberation is settled and memorialized—even writing the memorial document is not less than ten days, causing many matters to linger and delay—from now on this should not happen again.
translations.idiomatic: But because your views differ, cases are sent back repeatedly for reconsideration; even when deliberation is settled, drafting the memorial takes no less than ten days, causing many cases to linger—from now on this must cease.'

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「故廣甯尹高楨為政尚猛，雖小過，有杖而殺之者。

translations.literal: He also said: 'Former Guangning Administrator Gao Zhen in governing still favored severity; even for small faults, there were those staff-beaten to death.'
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'The former administrator of Guangning, Gao Zhen, governed with excessive severity, beating men to death even for minor faults.'

sentences.zh: 即罪至於死而情或可恕，猶當念之，況其小過者乎？

translations.literal: Even when the offense reaches death yet the circumstances may be pardonable, one should still reflect on it—how much more for small faults?
translations.idiomatic: Even when an offense warrants death yet the circumstances may warrant mercy, one should still reflect carefully—how much more so for minor faults?'

sentences.zh: 人之性命安可輕哉！

translations.literal: How can human life be treated lightly!
translations.idiomatic: How can human life be treated so lightly!'

sentences.zh: 」上以正隆《續降制書》多任己意，傷於苛察。

translations.literal: The emperor considered that the Zhenglong Continued Promulgated Regulatory Documents mostly followed personal whim, harmful in harsh scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that the Zhenglong Continued Promulgated Regulatory Documents too often followed personal whim and were excessively harsh.

sentences.zh: 而與皇統之《制》並用，是非淆亂，莫知適從，奸吏因得上下其手。

translations.literal: Yet they were used together with the Huangtong Regulations, right and wrong confused and mixed, none knowing what to follow; corrupt officials thereby could raise and lower their hands [manipulate outcomes].
translations.idiomatic: Used alongside the Huangtong Regulations, they created such confusion of standards that no one knew which code to follow, allowing corrupt officials to manipulate outcomes at will.

sentences.zh: 遂置局，命大理卿移剌綎總中外明法者共校正。

translations.literal: Thereupon they established a bureau, appointing the chief of the Office of Imperial Justice Yila Su to gather those versed in law within and without the court jointly to collate and correct.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon a bureau was established, and Chief of the Office of Imperial Justice Yila Su was charged with assembling legal experts from inside and outside the court to collate and revise the code.

sentences.zh: 乃以皇統、正隆之《制》及大定《軍前權宜條理》、後《續行條理》，倫其輕重，刪繁正失。

translations.literal: Then taking the Huangtong and Zhenglong Regulations together with the Dading Provisional Articles and Ordinances for Military Campaigns and the later Continued Operational Articles and Ordinances, they arranged their light and heavy, cut redundancy and corrected errors.
translations.idiomatic: They drew on the Huangtong and Zhenglong Regulations, the Dading Provisional Articles and Ordinances for Military Campaigns, and the later Continued Operational Articles and Ordinances, arranging punishments by severity while cutting redundancy and correcting errors.

sentences.zh: 制有闕者以律文足之。

translations.literal: Where the regulations had gaps, they supplemented them with statutory text.
translations.idiomatic: Where the regulations were incomplete, they supplemented them with statutory provisions.

sentences.zh: 制、律俱闕及疑而不能決者，則取旨畫定。

translations.literal: Where both regulations and statutes lacked provision and doubt could not be resolved, they then obtained imperial intent and fixed it by decree.
translations.idiomatic: Cases where both regulations and statutes were silent, or where doubt could not be resolved, were settled by obtaining the emperor's decision and issuing a definitive ruling.

sentences.zh: 《軍前權宜條理》內有可以常行者亦為定法，余未應者亦別為一部存之。

translations.literal: Within the Provisional Articles and Ordinances for Military Campaigns, those that could be regularly applied were also made fixed law; the remainder not yet applicable was also set apart as a separate fascicle and preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions within the Provisional Articles and Ordinances for Military Campaigns that could be applied on a standing basis were incorporated into permanent law; those not yet applicable were preserved in a separate fascicle.

sentences.zh: 參以近所定徒杖減半之法，凡校定千一百九十條，分為十二卷，以《大定重修制條》為名，詔頒行焉。

translations.literal: Referencing also the recently fixed method of halving penal servitude and beating, in all they collated and fixed 1,190 articles, divided into twelve fascicles, named the Recast Regulatory Articles of the Dading Era, and an edict ordered their promulgation.
translations.idiomatic: Incorporating the recently adopted rule halving penalties of penal servitude and beating, they finalized 1,190 articles in twelve fascicles under the title Recast Regulatory Articles of the Dading Era, and an edict ordered their promulgation throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 二十年，上見有蹂踐禾稼者，謂宰相曰：「今後有踐民田者杖六十，盜人穀者杖八十，並償其直。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, the emperor saw persons trampling crops and said to the chief ministers: 'Henceforth whoever tramples civilian fields shall receive sixty strokes of the staff; whoever steals another's grain shall receive eighty strokes, and in both cases shall compensate the full value.'
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, seeing people trampling crops in the fields, the emperor told his chief ministers: 'Henceforth anyone who treads upon a farmer's fields shall receive sixty strokes of the staff, and anyone who steals another's grain shall receive eighty, and in both cases shall pay full compensation.'

sentences.zh: 」二十一年，尚書省奏：「鞏州民馬俊妻安姐與管卓姦，俊以斧擊殺之，罪當死。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, the Department of State Affairs memorialized: 'Gong Prefecture commoner Ma Jun's wife Anjie committed adultery with Guan Zhuo; Jun struck and killed him with an axe—the offense warrants death.'
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, the Department of State Affairs reported: 'A commoner of Gong Prefecture, Ma Jun, learned that his wife Anjie had committed adultery with Guan Zhuo and killed him with an axe—a capital offense.'

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「可減死一等，以戒敗風俗者。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'His death penalty may be reduced by one grade, to warn those who ruin custom and morals.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'Reduce the death sentence by one grade, as a warning to those who corrupt public morals.'

sentences.zh: 」二十二年，上謂宰臣曰：「凡尚書省送大理寺文字，一斷便可聞奏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, the emperor told the chief ministers: 'All documents the Department of State Affairs sends to the Office of Imperial Justice, once decided may immediately be reported to Us.'
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, the emperor told his chief ministers: 'Whenever the Department of State Affairs forwards a case to the Office of Imperial Justice, a single adjudication should suffice for reporting to the throne.'

sentences.zh: 如烏古論公說事，近取觀之，初送法寺如法裁斷，再送司直披詳，又送闔寺參詳，反覆三次，妄生情見，不得結絕。

translations.literal: Take for example the Wugulun Gong affair—We recently examined it: first sent to the legal office for judgment according to law, again sent to the reviewing censor for detailed examination, again sent to the whole office for joint deliberation—back and forth three times, wantonly generating discretionary views, unable to bring closure.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the Wugulun Gong case, which We recently reviewed: it was first sent to the legal office for adjudication under the code, then to the reviewing censor for detailed scrutiny, then to the entire tribunal for joint deliberation—three rounds in all, during which discretionary interpretations were invented on every pass, and the case still could not be closed.

sentences.zh: 朕以國政不宜滯留，昨雖炙艾六百炷，未嘗一日不坐朝，欲使卿等知勤政也。

translations.literal: We hold that state affairs ought not linger; yesterday though We underwent moxibustion with six hundred cones, not one day did We fail to hold court, wishing to make you all know diligent governance.
translations.idiomatic: We hold that state business must not be delayed; though yesterday We underwent six hundred moxibustion treatments, We did not miss a single day of court, precisely so that you would understand what diligent governance requires.'

sentences.zh: 自今可止一次送寺，闔寺披詳，荀有情見即具以聞，毋使滯留也。

translations.literal: From now on send to the office only once; the whole office shall examine in detail—if there are discretionary views, report them fully; do not let matters linger.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth send each case to the tribunal only once for full deliberation; if discretionary views arise, report them completely, but do not allow cases to stagnate.'

sentences.zh: 」二十三年，尚書省奏：「益都民範德年七十六，為劉祐毆殺。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, the Department of State Affairs memorialized: 'Yidu commoner Fan De, age seventy-six, was beaten to death by Liu You.'
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, the Department of State Affairs reported: 'Fan De, a seventy-six-year-old commoner of Yidu, was beaten to death by Liu You.'

sentences.zh: 祐法當死，以祐父母年俱七十餘，家無侍丁，上請。

translations.literal: By law You merited death; because You's parents were both over seventy, and the household had no adult sons to serve them, they submitted a petition upward.
translations.idiomatic: You merited death under the law, but because both his parents were over seventy and the household had no adult son to support them, a petition for clemency was submitted.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「范德與祐父母年相若，自當如父母相待，至毆殺之，難議末減，其論如法。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Fan De and You's parents were of like age; he ought naturally to have treated them as parents—yet he beat one to death; it is hard to argue for final mitigation; decide according to law.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'Fan De was about the same age as You's parents and should have treated them with the deference owed to elders; that he beat one of them to death makes mitigation difficult—adjudicate strictly according to law.'

sentences.zh: 」尚書省奏招討司官及禿裏乞取本部財物制，上曰：「遠人止可矜恤，若進貢不闕，更以兵邀之，強取財物，與盜何異？

translations.literal: The Department of State Affairs memorialized on regulations for pacification commissioners and Tuli begging to take local goods; the emperor said: 'Remote peoples should only be treated with compassion; if their tribute is not lacking, yet troops are further sent to intercept them and goods forcibly taken—how is this different from robbery?'
translations.idiomatic: When the Department of State Affairs submitted regulations on pacification commissioners and Tuli envoys seizing local property, the emperor said: 'Frontier peoples deserve compassion; if their tribute obligations are met, to send troops to waylay them and seize their goods by force—how is that different from robbery?'

sentences.zh: 且或因而生事，何可不懲。

translations.literal: Moreover it may thereby give rise to incidents—how can it go unpunished?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, such conduct could easily provoke disturbances—how can it go unpunished?'

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「朕所行制條，皆臣下所奏行者，天下事多，人力有限，豈能一一盡之。

translations.literal: He also said: 'The regulatory articles We promulgate are all matters officials memorialized should be enacted; affairs under Heaven are many, human capacity is limited—how can one exhaust them all?'
translations.idiomatic: He added: 'The regulatory articles I promulgate are all measures officials have recommended; affairs across the realm are countless and human capacity finite—no ruler can anticipate every contingency.'

sentences.zh: 必因一事奏聞，方知有所窒礙，隨即更定。

translations.literal: Only when because of one matter a memorial is submitted does one know there is some obstruction, and immediately it is revised and fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Only when a specific case is reported do we discover where the law proves obstructive, and we revise it at once.'

sentences.zh: 今有聖旨、條理，復有制條，是使奸吏得以輕重也。

translations.literal: Now there are imperial edicts, articles and ordinances, and again regulatory articles—this allows corrupt officials to manipulate light and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now we have imperial edicts, administrative ordinances, and regulatory articles all at once—which only enables corrupt officials to manipulate penalties at will.'

sentences.zh: 」大興府民趙無事帶酒亂言，父千捕告，法當死。

translations.literal: A Daxing Prefecture commoner Zhao Wushi, drunk, spoke wildly; his father had him arrested and reported—the offense warranted death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wushi, a commoner of Daxing Prefecture, spoke treasonously while drunk; his father had him arrested and denounced him—a capital offense.'

sentences.zh: 上曰：「為父不恤其子而告捕之，其正如此，人所甚難。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'For a father not to pity his son yet arrest and report him—such righteousness is exceedingly hard for men.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'For a father to set aside pity for his own son and turn him in—such rectitude is truly difficult for any person to achieve.'

sentences.zh: 可特減死一等。

translations.literal: His death penalty may be specially reduced by one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce the death sentence by one grade as a special dispensation.'

sentences.zh: 」武器署丞奕、直長骨赧坐受草畔子財，奕杖八十，骨赧笞二十，監察御史梁襄等坐失糾察罰俸一月。

translations.literal: Weapons Office deputy director Yi and section chief Guhan were convicted of accepting Caobanzi's bribes; Yi received eighty strokes of the staff, Guhan twenty strokes of the bamboo, investigating censor Liang Xiang and others were convicted of failing to investigate and were fined one month's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Weapons Office Deputy Director Yi and Section Chief Guhan were convicted of accepting bribes from Caobanzi; Yi was sentenced to eighty strokes of the staff and Guhan to twenty strokes of the bamboo, while Investigating Censor Liang Xiang and others, convicted of failing to investigate, were fined one month's salary.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「監察，人君之耳目。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Investigating censors are the ruler's eyes and ears.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'Investigating censors are the monarch's eyes and ears.'

sentences.zh: 事由朕發，何以監察為？

translations.literal: When matters originate from Us, what need is there for investigating censors?
translations.idiomatic: If every case originates with me, what purpose do investigating censors serve?'

sentences.zh: 」上以法寺斷獄，以漢字譯女直字，會法又復各出情見，妄生穿鑿，徒致稽緩，遂詔罷情見。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the legal office in adjudicating cases translated Jurchen script into Chinese characters, and when applying law each again issued separate discretionary views, wantonly forcing strained constructions, merely causing delay, then decreed abolition of discretionary views.
translations.idiomatic: Because the legal office, when adjudicating cases, translated Jurchen records into Chinese and each judge then produced his own discretionary interpretation, inventing forced constructions that only delayed proceedings, the emperor decreed the abolition of discretionary views.

sentences.zh: 二十五年二月，上以婦人在囚，輸作不便，而杖不分決，與殺無異，遂命免死輸作者，決杖二百而免輸作，以臀、背分決。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, second month, the emperor, because women in custody found penal labor inconvenient, and undivided beating was no different from killing, then ordered those commuted from death to penal labor to receive two hundred strokes and be exempted from penal labor, with buttocks and back divided for beating.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twenty-fifth year, noting that imprisoned women could not conveniently perform penal labor and that undivided beating was tantamount to execution, the emperor ordered that those whose death sentences were commuted to penal labor should instead receive two hundred strokes divided between buttocks and back and be exempted from labor.

sentences.zh: 時後族有犯罪者，尚書省引「八議」奏，上曰：「法者，公天下持平之器，若親者犯而從減，是使之恃此而橫恣也。

translations.literal: At that time when a member of the empress's clan committed an offense, the Department of State Affairs cited the 'Eight Deliberations' in memorial; the emperor said: 'Law is the instrument that balances all under Heaven impartially; if relatives who offend receive reduction thereby, this makes them rely on it to act wantonly.'
translations.idiomatic: When a member of the empress's clan committed an offense and the Department of State Affairs invoked the Eight Deliberations, the emperor said: 'Law is the instrument by which the realm is held in impartial balance; if kinsmen of the throne may offend yet receive leniency, they will rely upon that privilege to act with impunity.'

sentences.zh: 昔漢文誅薄昭，有足取者。

translations.literal: In former times Emperor Wen of Han executed Bo Zhao—there is something worth taking from that.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Han put Bo Zhao to death, he showed the right way forward.'

sentences.zh: 前二十年時，後族濟州節度使烏林達鈔兀嘗犯大辟，朕未嘗宥。

translations.literal: Twenty years ago, empress-clan Jizhou military governor Wulin Da Chaowu once committed the great penalty—We never pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years ago, Wulin Da Chaowu of the empress's clan, then military governor of Jizhou, committed a capital offense, and I did not grant him clemency.'

sentences.zh: 今乃宥之，是開後世輕重出入之門也。

translations.literal: Now to pardon him is to open the gate for future ages of manipulating light and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: To pardon him now would open the door for future generations to manipulate the severity of punishment at will.'

sentences.zh: 」宰臣曰：「古所以議親，尊天子，別庶人也。

translations.literal: The chief ministers said: 'Anciently the reason for deliberating kin was to honor the Son of Heaven and distinguish the common people.'
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers replied: 'The ancients instituted deliberation for kinship to honor the Son of Heaven and distinguish the imperial house from commoners.'

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「外家自異於宗室，漢外戚權太重，至移國祚，朕所以不令諸王、公主有權也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'The maternal clan is naturally distinct from the imperial house; Han consort kin held power too heavy, even to the shifting of the dynastic mandate—therefore We do not allow imperial princes and princesses to hold power.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: 'The maternal clan is naturally distinct from the imperial house; in Han times consort kin wielded such power that the throne itself was overturned—which is why I have refused to grant real authority to imperial princes and princesses.'

sentences.zh: 夫有功于國，議勳可也。

translations.literal: Now for merit toward the state, deliberating merit is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Those who have rendered distinguished service to the state may claim deliberation for merit.'

sentences.zh: 至若議賢，既曰賢矣，肯犯法乎？

translations.literal: As for deliberating worthiness—as to worthiness, would one willing offend against law?
translations.idiomatic: As for deliberation for worthiness—if a man is truly worthy, would he violate the law?'

sentences.zh: 脫或緣坐，則固當減請也。

translations.literal: If perchance by guilt through association, then one should properly petition for reduction.
translations.idiomatic: If he is implicated only by association, then a petition for mitigation is entirely appropriate.'

sentences.zh: 」二十六年，遂奏定太子妃大功以上親，及與皇家無服者、及賢而犯私罪者，皆不入議。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, they then memorialized fixing that the crown prince's consort's kin within great mourning, and those without mourning obligation toward the imperial house, and the worthy who commit private offenses—all are not admitted to deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, it was decreed that relatives of the crown prince's consort within the degree of great mourning, persons bearing no mourning obligation toward the imperial house, and those deemed worthy who commit private offenses—all were excluded from the Eight Deliberations.'

sentences.zh: 上謂宰臣曰：「法有倫而不倫者，其改定之。

translations.literal: The emperor told the chief ministers: 'Where law has principle yet lacks principle, revise and fix it.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his chief ministers: 'Where the law follows principle in some cases but violates it in others, revise it accordingly.'

sentences.zh: 」監察御史陶鈞以攜妓游北苑，歌飲池島間，迫近殿廷，提控官石玠聞而發之。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Tao Jun, taking courtesans to roam the Northern Park, singing and drinking among ponds and islets, approaching near the palace precincts—surveillance officer Shi Jie heard and exposed it.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Tao Jun was found to have escorted courtesans through the Northern Park, singing and drinking among its ponds and islets in proximity to the palace halls; Surveillance Officer Shi Jie heard of it and reported the affair.

sentences.zh: 鈞令其友閻恕 屬玠得緩。

translations.literal: Jun had his friend Yan Shu ask Shi Jie to obtain leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Jun had his friend Yan Shu intercede with Shi Jie to secure lenient handling.

sentences.zh: 既而事覺，法司奏，當徒二年半。

translations.literal: When the matter came to light, the legal office memorialized that the penalty should be penal servitude two and a half years.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair came to light, the legal authorities recommended penal servitude of two and a half years.

sentences.zh: 詔以鈞耳目之官，攜妓入禁苑，無上下之分，杖六十，玠、恕皆坐之。

translations.literal: An edict held that Jun, as an organ of the ruler's senses, bringing courtesans into the forbidden park, showed no distinction of superior and subordinate—sixty strokes of the staff; Shi and Yan were both convicted as well.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ruled that Tao Jun, as an imperial censor, had violated the distinction of rank by bringing courtesans into the forbidden park and sentenced him to sixty strokes of the staff; Shi Jie and Yan Shu were also convicted.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，上以制條拘於舊律，間有難解之詞，命刪修明白，使人皆曉之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, the emperor, because regulatory articles were constrained by old statutes and occasionally had difficult-to-understand language, ordered deletion and revision to clarity so all people would understand.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, finding that regulatory articles were hobbled by archaic statutory language and contained passages difficult to understand, the emperor ordered them revised into clear language so that everyone could comprehend the law.

sentences.zh: 舊禁民不得收制書，恐滋告訐之弊，章宗大定二十九年，言事者乞許民藏之。

translations.literal: Formerly common people were forbidden to collect regulatory documents, fearing the abuse of malicious denunciation; under Zhangzong in the twenty-ninth year of Dading, memorialists requested permission for common people to keep them.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners had long been forbidden to possess copies of the regulatory code, for fear of encouraging vexatious denunciations; in the twenty-ninth year of Dading, during Zhangzong's reign, memorialists petitioned to allow the populace to keep legal texts.

sentences.zh: 平章張汝霖曰：「昔子產鑄刑書，叔向譏之者，蓋不欲預使民測其輕重也。

translations.literal: Grand Counselor Zhang Rulin said: 'Formerly when Zichan cast penal books, Shu Xiang mocked him—he did not wish beforehand to let people gauge light and heavy.'
translations.idiomatic: Grand Counselor Zhang Rulin argued: 'When Zichan cast the penal statutes on bronze, Shu Xiang criticized him because he did not wish to let the people anticipate the severity of punishments in advance.'

sentences.zh: 今著不刊之典，使民曉然知之，猶江、河之易避而難犯，足以輔治，不禁為便。

translations.literal: Now inscribing an immutable canon, making people clearly know it, is like rivers easy to avoid yet hard to transgress—sufficient to assist governance; not forbidding is convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Publishing an immutable legal canon so that the people understand it clearly is like marking a river—easy to avoid and hard to violate—and would serve governance well; lifting the prohibition would be the better course.'

sentences.zh: 」以眾議多不欲，詔姑令仍舊禁之。

translations.literal: Because the multitude's deliberation mostly did not wish it, an edict ordered for the time being still to forbid as before.
translations.idiomatic: Because most officials opposed the change, an edict maintained the existing prohibition for the time being.

sentences.zh: 明昌元年，上問宰臣曰：「今何不專用律文？

translations.literal: In the first year of Mingchang, the emperor asked the chief ministers: 'Why now do We not exclusively use statutory text?'
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Mingchang, the emperor asked his chief ministers: 'Why do we not rely exclusively on the statutory code?'

sentences.zh: 」平章政事張汝霖曰：「前代律與令各有分，其有犯令，以律決之。

translations.literal: Grand Counselor Zhang Rulin said: 'Former ages' statutes and ordinances each had division; when one violated ordinances, statutes decided it.'
translations.idiomatic: Grand Counselor Zhang Rulin replied: 'In earlier dynasties statutes and administrative ordinances served distinct functions; violations of ordinances were adjudicated under the statutes.'

sentences.zh: 今國家制、律混淆，固當分也。

translations.literal: Now the state's regulations and statutes are confused and mixed—surely they should be divided.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty regulations and statutes have become intermingled, and they ought to be separated.'

sentences.zh: 」遂置詳定所，命審定律、令。

translations.literal: Thereupon they established a detailed review office and ordered examination and fixing of statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: A detailed review office was therefore established and charged with examining and revising the statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 承安二年，制軍前受財法，一貫以下，徒二年，以上徒三年，十貫處死。

translations.literal: In the second year of Cheng'an, they regulated law for receiving goods before the army: one string or below, penal servitude two years; above that penal servitude three years; ten strings merited death.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Cheng'an, a law was enacted for accepting bribes in the field: one string of cash or less warranted two years of penal servitude; more than one string warranted three years; ten strings warranted execution.

sentences.zh: 符寶典書北京奴盜符寶局金牌，伏誅，仍除屬籍。

translations.literal: Keeper of Seals and Talismans Beijing Nu stole the golden plaques of the Seals and Talismans Bureau, was executed, and still was removed from clan register.
translations.idiomatic: Beijing Nu, Keeper of Seals and Talismans, was executed for stealing the golden plaques from the Seals and Talismans Bureau and was struck from the clan register.

sentences.zh: 按虎、阿虎帶失覺察，各杖七十。

translations.literal: An Hu and A Hudai for failure of awareness each received seventy strokes of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: An Hu and A Hudai, convicted of negligent oversight, each received seventy strokes of the staff.

sentences.zh: 泰和二年，御史臺奏：「監察御史史肅言，《大定條理》：自二十年十一月四日以前，奴娶良人女為妻者，並准已娶為定，若夫亡，拘放從其主。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe, the Censorate memorialized: 'Investigating censor Shi Su stated: The Dading Articles and Ordinances: before the fourth day of the eleventh month of the twentieth year, slaves who married commoner women as wives—all approved as already married and fixed; if the husband died, detain or release according to their master.'
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taihe, the Censorate reported: 'Investigating Censor Shi Su noted that under the Dading Articles and Ordinances, slaves who had married commoner women before the fourth day of the eleventh month of the twentieth year were recognized as lawfully married; if the husband died, the woman was to be detained or released at the discretion of her master.'

sentences.zh: 離夫摘賣者令本主收贖，依舊與夫同聚。

translations.literal: Those separated from husbands and resold—the original master should redeem, and as before live together with the husband.
translations.idiomatic: If a woman was sold apart from her husband, the original owner was to redeem her and she would continue to live with her husband as before.

sentences.zh: 放良從良者即聽贖換，如未贖換間與夫所生男女並聽為良。

translations.literal: Those manumitted or following to commoner status might immediately be heard for redemption and exchange; if not yet redeemed and exchanged, the children born to the husband—all heard as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Manumitted persons could be redeemed and exchanged immediately; any children born to the couple before redemption was completed were recognized as commoners.

sentences.zh: 而《泰和新格》復以夫亡服除准良人例，離夫摘賣及放夫為良者，並聽為良。

translations.literal: But the Taihe New Regulations again took husband's death and mourning completion to follow commoner precedent; separated from husband, resold, and husbands manumitted to commoner status—all heard as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: But the Taihe New Regulations further held that after a husband's death and the completion of mourning, commoner precedent applied, and that women sold apart from their husbands or whose husbands had been manumitted were all to be recognized as commoners.

sentences.zh: 若未出離再配與奴，或雜奸所生男女並許為良。

translations.literal: If not yet separated and again matched to a slave, or children born of illicit intercourse—all permitted as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Women not yet formally separated who were remarried to slaves, and any children born of illicit unions, were also granted commoner status.

sentences.zh: 如此不同，皆編格官妄為增減，以致隨處訴訟紛擾，是涉違枉。

translations.literal: Such mutual differences—all from compilation officers wantonly adding and subtracting, causing everywhere lawsuits and confusion—this involves violation and perversion.
translations.idiomatic: Such inconsistencies arose because compiling officials had arbitrarily added and deleted provisions, provoking litigation and disorder everywhere—a clear violation of proper procedure.

sentences.zh: 」敕付所司正之。

translations.literal: An imperial command was delivered to the responsible office to correct it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the responsible authorities to rectify the discrepancies.'

sentences.zh: 初，詔凡條格入制文內者，分為別卷。

translations.literal: Initially, an edict ordered that all regulatory grids entering regulatory text should be divided into separate fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, an edict ordered that all supplementary regulations incorporated into the regulatory code be published as separate fascicles.

sentences.zh: 復詔制與律文輕重不同，及律所無者，各校定以聞。

translations.literal: Again an edict ordered that where regulations and statutory text differed in light and heavy, and what statutes lacked—each collate and fix and report.
translations.idiomatic: A further edict directed that wherever regulations and statutory provisions differed in severity, or where the statutes were silent, each discrepancy should be collated, resolved, and reported.

sentences.zh: 如禁屠宰之類，當著於令也，慎之勿忽，律令一定，不可更矣。

translations.literal: Such matters as prohibiting slaughter ought to be placed in ordinances—be careful, do not neglect; once statutes and ordinances are fixed, they cannot be changed again.
translations.idiomatic: Matters such as prohibitions on slaughter belong in the ordinances—take care not to neglect them; once statutes and ordinances are finalized, they must not be altered again.'

sentences.zh: 明昌三年七月，右司郎中孫鐸先以詳定所校《名例篇》進，既而諸篇皆成，復命中都路轉運使王寂、大理卿董師中等重校之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of Mingchang, Right Bureau director Sun Duo first submitted the Detailed Review Office's collated General Principles fascicle; thereafter all fascicles were complete, and again they ordered Metropolitan Circuit transport commissioner Wang Ji, Office of Imperial Justice chief Dong Shizhong and others to recollate.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year of Mingchang, Sun Duo of the Right Bureau submitted the collated General Principles fascicle from the Detailed Review Office; when all fascicles were complete, Wang Ji, transport commissioner of the Metropolitan Circuit, Chief Dong Shizhong of the Office of Imperial Justice, and others were appointed to conduct a further review.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，上以諸路枷杖多不如法，平章政事守貞曰：「枷杖尺寸有制，提刑兩月一巡察，必不敢違法也。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year, the emperor, because cangues and staffs in various circuits mostly did not accord with law, Grand Counselor Shouzhen said: 'Cangue and staff dimensions have regulation; investigative commissioners once every two months inspect—surely they dare not violate law.'
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year, noting that cangues and beating staves across the circuits often failed to meet statutory standards, Grand Counselor Shouzhen said: 'The dimensions of cangues and staves are prescribed by law, and investigative commissioners inspect every two months—officials will not dare violate the regulations.'

sentences.zh: 」五年正月，復令鉤校制、律，即付詳定所。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, they again ordered comparison and verification of regulations and statutes, immediately delivering to the Detailed Review Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, a further order directed comparison and verification of regulations against statutes, with the work assigned to the Detailed Review Office.

sentences.zh: 時詳定官言：「若依重修制文為式，則條目增減，罪名輕重，當異於律。

translations.literal: At that time the detailed review officers said: 'If following the recast regulatory text as model, then articles added and reduced, offense names light and heavy, would differ from statutes.'
translations.idiomatic: The detailed review officers observed: 'If we took the recast regulatory text as our template, the articles would differ from the statutes in both their number and the severity of the penalties assigned.'

sentences.zh: 既定復與舊同頒，則使人惑而易為奸矣！

translations.literal: Once fixed yet again promulgated together with the old, then it would make people confused and easy to commit corruption!
translations.idiomatic: To promulgate the new code alongside the old would only confuse the people and invite abuse!'

sentences.zh: 臣等謂，用今制條，參酌時宜，准律文修定，歷采前代刑書宜於今者，以補遺闕，取《刑統》疏文以釋之，著為常法，名曰《明昌律義》。

translations.literal: We your subjects propose: using present regulatory articles, consulting timely appropriateness, following statutory text to revise and fix, through the ages gathering former ages' penal books suitable for today to supplement omissions and gaps, taking the Tang Statutes and Comprehensive Regulations expository text to explain them, establishing as permanent law, named the Mingchang Legal Commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: We propose instead to take the current regulatory articles, adapt them to present needs, and revise them in accordance with statutory principles, drawing on penal codes of earlier dynasties wherever applicable to fill gaps, and using the expository commentaries of the Tang Statutes and Comprehensive Regulations for clarification—establishing this as permanent law under the title Mingchang Legal Commentaries.'

sentences.zh: 別編榷貨、邊部、權宜等事，集為《敕條》。

translations.literal: Separately compiling monopoly goods, frontier regions, provisional measures and such matters, collected as Imperial Decree Articles.
translations.idiomatic: Monopoly goods, frontier administration, and provisional measures would be compiled separately as the Imperial Decree Articles.'

sentences.zh: 」宰臣謂：「先所定令文尚有未完，俟皆通定，然後頒行。

translations.literal: The chief ministers said: 'The ordinances previously fixed still have incompleteness—wait until all are thoroughly fixed, then promulgate.'
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers replied: 'The administrative ordinances previously drafted remain incomplete; wait until the entire code is finalized before promulgation.'

sentences.zh: 若律科舉人，則止習舊律。

translations.literal: As for statute examination candidates, then only study old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates for the legal examination should continue to study the old statutes for the time being.'

sentences.zh: 」遂以知大興府事尼厖古鑒、御史中丞董師中、翰林待制奧屯忠孝小字牙哥，提點司天臺張嗣、翰林修撰完顏撒剌、刑部員外郎李庭義、大理丞麻安上為校定官，大理卿閻公貞，戶部侍郎李敬義、工部郎中賈鉉為覆定官，重修新律焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon they appointed as collating officers: Daxing Prefecture intendant Niimugua Jian, vice censor-in-chief Dong Shizhong, Hanlin awaiting appointment Ouchun Zhongxiao (courtesy name Yage), Directorate of Astronomy intendant Zhang Si, Hanlin reviser Wanyan Sala, Ministry of Justice vice director Li Tingyi, Office of Imperial Justice assistant chief Ma Anshang; as reviewing officers: Office of Imperial Justice chief Yan Gongzhen, Ministry of Revenue vice minister Li Jingyi, Ministry of Works director Jia Xuan—to recast the new statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Niimugua Jian, intendant of Daxing Prefecture; Vice Censor-in-Chief Dong Shizhong; Hanlin Attendant-Draftsman Ouchun Zhongxiao (courtesy name Yage); Zhang Si, intendant of the Directorate of Astronomy; Hanlin Reviser Wanyan Sala; Li Tingyi, vice director of the Ministry of Justice; and Ma Anshang, assistant chief of the Office of Imperial Justice were appointed collating officers; Chief Yan Gongzhen of the Office of Imperial Justice, Vice Minister Li Jingyi of the Ministry of Revenue, and Director Jia Xuan of the Ministry of Works were appointed reviewing officers, and the work of recasting the new code commenced.

sentences.zh: 時奏獄而法官有獨出情見者，上曰：「或言法官不當出情見，故論者紛紛不已。

translations.literal: At that time when reporting cases and legal officers had those singly issuing discretionary views; the emperor said: 'Some say legal officers ought not issue discretionary views, therefore debaters argue endlessly.'
translations.idiomatic: When a case came before the throne and a judge offered an independent discretionary interpretation, the emperor remarked: 'Some claim judges should not issue discretionary views, and the debate has continued without end.'

sentences.zh: 朕謂情見非出於法外，但折衷以從法爾。

translations.literal: We hold discretionary views are not outside law, but only balancing the middle to follow law.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that discretionary views do not operate outside the law, but seek a balanced reading that conforms to it.'

sentences.zh: 」平章守貞曰：「是制自大定二十三年罷之。

translations.literal: Grand Counselor Shouzhen said: 'That system since Dading twenty-third year was abolished.'
translations.idiomatic: Grand Counselor Shouzhen noted: 'That practice was abolished in the twenty-third year of Dading.'

sentences.zh: 然律有起請諸條，是古亦許情見矣。

translations.literal: Yet statutes have petition-initiated articles—thus antiquity also permitted discretionary views.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the statutes contain provisions for submitted petitions, which shows that discretionary views were permitted even in antiquity.'

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「科條有限，而人情無窮，情見亦豈可無也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Statutory articles are limited, yet human circumstances are infinite—how can discretionary views be absent?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: 'Statutory provisions are finite, but human circumstances are infinite—how can discretionary views be dispensed with?'

sentences.zh: 」明昌五年，尚書省奏：「在制，《名例》內徒年之律，無決杖之文便不用杖。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Mingchang, the Department of State Affairs memorialized: 'In the regulations, within General Principles the statute on years of penal servitude—with no text on deciding beating, then do not use beating.'
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Mingchang, the Department of State Affairs reported: 'Under current regulations, the General Principles section governing years of penal servitude contains no provision for accompanying beatings, and beatings have therefore been omitted.'

sentences.zh: 緣先謂流刑非今所宜，且代流役四年以上俱決杖，而徒三年以下難復不用。

translations.literal: Because formerly they held exile penalty was not suitable for now, and moreover substituting for exile labor four years and above all had beating decided, yet penal servitude three years and below was hard again not to use.
translations.idiomatic: Exile was previously deemed unsuitable for our times, and penal servitude of four years or more substituted for exile with accompanying beatings, but it seems inconsistent not to apply beatings to penal servitude of three years or less.'

sentences.zh: 婦人比之男子雖差輕 ，亦當例減。

translations.literal: Women compared to men though somewhat lighter, should also by precedent be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Although punishments for women are somewhat lighter than for men, they should be reduced by the same proportional rule.'

sentences.zh: 」遂以徒二年以下者杖六十，二年以上杖七十，婦人犯者並決五十，著於《敕條》。

translations.literal: Thereupon for penal servitude two years and below, sixty strokes; two years and above, seventy strokes; women offenders all decided fifty strokes—placed in Imperial Decree Articles.
translations.idiomatic: It was therefore decreed that penal servitude of two years or less would be accompanied by sixty strokes of the staff, penal servitude of more than two years by seventy strokes, and female offenders by fifty strokes in all cases, as recorded in the Imperial Decree Articles.'

sentences.zh: 承安三年，敕尚書省：「自今特旨事，如律令程式者，始可送部。

translations.literal: In the third year of Cheng'an, an edict to the Department of State Affairs: 'From now on special-imperial-intent matters—only those like statutes and ordinances in procedure may be sent to the ministries.'
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Cheng'an, an edict to the Department of State Affairs directed: 'Henceforth only imperial directives that follow established statutory and administrative procedure may be forwarded to the ministries.'

sentences.zh: 自餘創行之事，但召部官赴省議之。

translations.literal: As for remaining newly initiated matters, merely summon ministry officials to come to the Department to deliberate.
