translations.idiomatic: All other newly initiated measures should be discussed by convening ministry officials at the Department of State Affairs.'

sentences.zh: 」四年四月，尚書省請再覆定令文，上因敕宰臣曰：「凡事理明白者轉奏可也。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, fourth month, the Department of State Affairs requested again to review-fix ordinance text; the emperor thereupon charged the chief ministers: 'Whatever the principle is clear may be reported onward.'
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year, when the Department of State Affairs requested a further review of the administrative ordinances, the emperor instructed the chief ministers: 'Matters that are clear in principle may be reported directly to the throne.'

sentences.zh: 文牘多者恐難遍覽，其三推情疑以聞。

translations.literal: Where documents are many, fearing difficulty in comprehensive perusal, thrice extend circumstance and doubt and report.
translations.idiomatic: Cases with extensive documentation may be difficult to review in full—in those instances, submit up to three rounds of reasoning on points of doubt.'

sentences.zh: 」五月，上以法不適平，常行杖樣，多不能用。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the emperor, because the law did not suit fairness, the regular staff pattern—many could not use it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, the emperor found that existing beating standards were neither fair nor practical and were widely ignored in practice.

sentences.zh: 遂定分寸，鑄銅為杖式，頒之天下。

translations.literal: Thereupon fixing dimensions and inches, casting bronze as staff pattern, promulgating throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered precise dimensions established, bronze beating rods cast to standard, and the model promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「若以笞杖太輕，恐情理有難恕者，訊杖可再議之。

translations.literal: And said: 'If because bamboo and staff are too light, fearing circumstances hard to pardon, interrogation staff may be again deliberated.'
translations.idiomatic: He added: 'If the lighter bamboo and staff punishments prove inadequate for offenders whose circumstances merit no mercy, the standard for interrogation beatings may be reconsidered.'

sentences.zh: 」五年五月，刑部員外郎馬復言：「外官尚苛刻者不遵銅杖式，輒用大杖，多致人死。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, fifth month, Ministry of Justice vice director Ma Fu stated: 'Outside officials still harsh and severe do not follow the bronze staff pattern, rashly using large staves—many causing people's death.'
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year, Ma Fu, vice director of the Ministry of Justice, reported: 'Some local officials, still inclined to severity, ignore the bronze staff standard and arbitrarily use heavier staves, often beating prisoners to death.'

sentences.zh: 」詔令按察司糾劾黜之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the investigative commission to impeach and dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed the investigative commissions to impeach and dismiss such officials.'

sentences.zh: 先嘗令諸死囚及除名罪，所委官相去二百里外，並犯徒以下逮及二十人以上者，並令其官就讞之。

translations.literal: Formerly they had ordered: all death-row prisoners and removal-of-name offenses, where appointed officials were distant two hundred li apart, and all reaching penal servitude and below totaling twenty persons and above—all ordered those officials to adjudicate on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, an order had required that capital cases and offenses warranting removal from official registers, cases in which the appointed officials were more than two hundred li apart, and any case involving twenty or more offenders sentenced to penal servitude or below—all be adjudicated on the spot by the assigned officials.

sentences.zh: 刑部員外郎完顏綱言：「自是制行，如上京最近之地往還不下三、二千里，如北京留守司亦動經數月，愈致稽留，未便。

translations.literal: Ministry of Justice vice director Wanyan Gang stated: 'Since this regulation was enacted, even the nearest places such as Shangjing—round trip not less than three or two thousand li; such as Beijing Retention Office also often several months—increasingly causing delay, not convenient.'
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Gang, vice director of the Ministry of Justice, argued: 'Since this regulation took effect, even the nearest jurisdictions such as Shangjing require round trips of two or three thousand li, and cases referred to the Beijing Retention Office routinely take months—resulting in even greater delays.'

sentences.zh: 」詔復從舊，令委官追取鞫之。

translations.literal: An edict restored following the old, ordering appointed officials to pursue and summon for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored the previous practice, directing assigned officials to summon defendants for interrogation as before.'

sentences.zh: 十二月，翰林修撰楊庭秀言：「州縣官往往以權勢自居，喜怒自任，聽訟之際，鮮克加審。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Hanlin reviser Yang Tingxiu stated: 'Prefecture and county officials often take authority and power as their own position, joy and anger as self-willed; when hearing lawsuits, rarely able to add careful examination.'
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Yang Tingxiu, Hanlin Reviser, reported: 'Prefectural and county magistrates often wield their authority arbitrarily, indulging personal caprice; when hearing cases, they rarely examine the evidence with care.'

sentences.zh: 但使譯人往來傳詞，罪之輕重，成於其口，貨賂公行，冤者至有三、二十年不能正者。

translations.literal: Merely making translators go back and forth transmitting words—the light and heavy of offense settled by their mouths; bribes openly practiced; the wronged even up to twenty or thirty years unable to be rectified.
translations.idiomatic: They rely on interpreters to relay testimony back and forth, leaving the severity of the sentence entirely to the interpreter's word; bribery is rampant, and the wrongfully convicted may wait twenty or thirty years without redress.'

sentences.zh: 」上遂命定立條約，違者按察司糾之。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon ordered establishment of fixed covenants; violators the investigative commission shall impeach.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon ordered formal regulations established, with violators subject to impeachment by the investigative commissions.'

sentences.zh: 且謂宰臣曰：「長貳官委幕職及司吏推問獄囚，命申御史臺聞奏之制，當復舉行也。

translations.literal: Moreover he told the chief ministers: 'The regulation requiring senior deputies' subordinates and clerks who interrogate prisoners to report through the Censorate for imperial hearing—should be restored and implemented.'
translations.idiomatic: He also told his chief ministers: 'The regulation requiring senior deputies' clerks who interrogate prisoners to report through the Censorate should be revived and enforced.'

sentences.zh: 」又命編前後條制，書之於冊，以備將來考驗。

translations.literal: He also ordered compiling the former and latter regulatory provisions, writing them in booklets, to prepare for future examination and verification.
translations.idiomatic: He further ordered that past and present regulations be compiled into registers for future reference.'

sentences.zh: 泰和元年正月，尚書省奏，以見行銅杖式輕細，奸宄不畏，遂命有司量所犯用大杖，且禁不得過五分。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Taihe, the Secretariat memorialized that because the current bronze staff pattern was light and fine, wicked evildoers did not fear; they then ordered responsible offices to measure offenses and use large staves, and forbade exceeding five-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Taihe, the Secretariat reported that because the current bronze staff standard was too light, criminals no longer feared it; officials were ordered to use heavier staves according to the severity of offenses, but not to exceed half the statutory maximum.

sentences.zh: 十二月，所修律成，凡十有二篇：一曰《名例》，二曰《衛禁》，三曰《職制》，四曰《戶婚》五曰《廄庫》，六曰《擅興》，七曰《賊盜》，八曰《鬥訟》，九曰《詐偽》，十曰《雜律》，十一曰《捕亡》，十二曰《斷獄》。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the revised statutes were completed, twelve sections in all: first General Principles; second Palace Security; third Official Regulations; fourth Households and Marriage; fifth Stables and Storehouses; sixth Unauthorized Enterprises; seventh Theft and Robbery; eighth Assault and Litigation; ninth Fraud and Forgery; tenth Miscellaneous Statutes; eleventh Apprehension of Fugitives; twelfth Judgment of Cases.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the revised code was completed, comprising twelve sections: General Principles, Palace Security, Official Regulations, Households and Marriage, Stables and Storehouses, Unauthorized Enterprises, Theft and Robbery, Assault and Litigation, Fraud and Forgery, Miscellaneous Statutes, Apprehension of Fugitives, and Judgment of Cases.

sentences.zh: 實《唐律》也，但加贖銅皆倍之，增徒至四年、五年為七，削不宜於時者四十七條，增時用之制百四十九條，因而略有所損益者二百八十有二條，餘百二十六條皆從其舊。

translations.literal: It was in fact the Tang Code, but all copper ransom payments were doubled; penal servitude of four and five years was increased to seven; forty-seven articles unsuited to the times were deleted; one hundred forty-nine timely regulations were added; two hundred eighty-two articles were revised with minor adjustments; the remaining one hundred twenty-six articles followed the original.
translations.idiomatic: It was essentially the Tang Code, but all copper ransom payments were doubled, and penal servitude of four and five years was extended to seven; forty-seven articles unsuited to the age were deleted, one hundred forty-nine timely provisions were added, two hundred eighty-two were revised in minor respects, and the remaining one hundred twenty-six were left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 又加以分其一為二、分其一為四者六條，凡五百六十三條，為三十卷，附注以明其事，疏義以釋其疑，名曰《泰和律義》。

translations.literal: Additionally six articles were created by splitting one into two or one into four; in all five hundred sixty-three articles in thirty fascicles, with appended notes to clarify matters and commentary to resolve doubts, named the Taihe Legal Commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Six further articles were created by subdividing existing ones; in all there were five hundred sixty-three articles in thirty fascicles, with appended notes to clarify particulars and commentary to resolve ambiguities, under the title Taihe Legal Commentaries.

sentences.zh: 自《官品令》、《職員令》之下，曰《祠令》四十八條，《戶令》六十六條，《學令》十一條，《選舉令》八十三條，《封爵令》九條、《封贈令》十條，《宮衛令》十條，《軍防令》二十五條，《儀制令》二十三條，《衣服令》十條，《公式令》五十八條，《祿令》十七條，《倉庫令》七條，《廄牧令》十二條，《田令》十七條，《賦役令》二十三條，《關市令》十三條，《捕亡令》二十條，《賞令》二十五條，《醫疾令》五條，《假寧令》十四條，《獄官令》百有六條，《雜令》四十九條，《釋道令》十條，《營繕令》十三條，《河防令》十一條，《服制令》十一條，附以年月之制，曰《律令》二十卷。

translations.literal: Below the Official Rank Ordinance and Staff Ordinance were: the Sacrificial Ordinance forty-eight articles, Household Ordinance sixty-six, School Ordinance eleven, Selection Ordinance eighty-three, Enfeoffment Ordinance nine, Posthumous Enfeoffment Ordinance ten, Palace Guard Ordinance ten, Military Defense Ordinance twenty-five, Ritual Ordinance twenty-three, Garment Ordinance ten, Formula Ordinance fifty-eight, Salary Ordinance seventeen, Granary Ordinance seven, Stable and Pasturage Ordinance twelve, Field Ordinance seventeen, Tax and Corvée Ordinance twenty-three, Pass and Market Ordinance thirteen, Apprehension Ordinance twenty, Reward Ordinance twenty-five, Medical Ordinance five, Leave Ordinance fourteen, Prison Official Ordinance one hundred six, Miscellaneous Ordinance forty-nine, Buddhist and Daoist Ordinance ten, Construction Ordinance thirteen, River Defense Ordinance eleven, Mourning Garment Ordinance eleven—with calendrical provisions appended, called the Statutes and Ordinances in twenty fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Below the ordinances on official ranks and staffing came twenty-six further ordinances: Sacrificial (48 articles), Household (66), School (11), Selection and Appointment (83), Enfeoffment (9), Posthumous Enfeoffment (10), Palace Guard (10), Military Defense (25), Ritual Protocol (23), Garments (10), Administrative Formulas (58), Salaries (17), Granaries (7), Stables and Pasturage (12), Land (17), Tax and Corvée (23), Passes and Markets (13), Apprehension (20), Rewards (25), Medicine (5), Leave (14), Prison Administration (106), Miscellaneous (49), Buddhism and Daoism (10), Construction (13), River Defense (11), and Mourning Garments (11)—with calendrical provisions appended, all collected as the Statutes and Ordinances in twenty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 又定《制敕》九十五條，《榷貨》八十五條，《蕃部》三十九條，曰《新定敕條》三卷，《六部格式》三十卷。

translations.literal: Also fixed were the Regulatory Edicts ninety-five articles, Monopoly Goods eighty-five, Frontier Peoples thirty-nine—called the Newly Fixed Imperial Decree Articles in three fascicles, and the Six Departments Formats in thirty fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Also codified were ninety-five Regulatory Edicts, eighty-five articles on state monopolies, and thirty-nine on frontier peoples, collected as the Newly Fixed Imperial Decree Articles in three fascicles, together with the Six Departments Formats in thirty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 司空襄以進，詔以明年五月頒行之。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Xiang presented it; an edict ordered promulgation in the fifth month of the following year.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Xiang presented the completed code, and an edict ordered its promulgation in the fifth month of the following year.
